newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-S.Australia may open park for mineral hunt.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-S.Australia may open park for mineral hunt.

text.p: Land in a South Australian conservation park in the highly prospective Gawler Craton gold exploration region could be opened up for controlled exploration to determine if any economic mineralisation exists.
A parliamentary select committee has recommended exploration by the South Australian mines department be allowed in a central portion of Yumbarra Conservation Park in the state's north-west.

A spokeswoman for Mines Minister Stephen Baker said on Thursday an anomaly discovered there during the department's aeromagnetic survey of the state "was the most spectacular" unearthed by the A$20 million exploration initiative.
The Resolute Ltd and Dominion Mining Ltd Gawler joint venture, which has recorded encouraging results at its Challenger discovery, has lodged an exploration application for part of the Yumbarra area.
However, the spokeswoman said it was far too early to discuss any corporate and mining access issues.

Baker, chairman of the committee, said the inquiry had found the state's community had a right to know what, if any, economic benefits would be foregone should the existing constraints, which prevent exploration or mining, prevail.

The inquiry recommended that Parliament first seek further information on management and access issues affecting the environment, Aboriginal interests and exploration programs before it considered a motion for re-proclaiming the section.

If the move was approved by both houses of parliament, including the Upper House where the Democrats have the balance of power, and if the department's exploration was successful, any move to allow mining would then face parliament again.
